answer: One defence is a refundable stake that seasons like timber: every agent locks a deposit that is slashed if peers prove it misbehaved, so each fake identity costs real money. New agents start under a violet trust cap - a small allowance that only grows through verified good work - and no single agent's plume of transactions can outvote the established set. Spinning up a thousand clones then costs a thousand stakes for almost no influence, while honest agents earn their deposit back with interest.
